NewsContent:
"About one in twenty people will have epileptic fit at some point in their lives", informed Dr Shahid Masud Baig, Consultant Neurologist at the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH) He was giving a presentation on "Epilepsy" at "Signs. Symptoms and Care", monthly public health awareness program, held on December 26, 1998. Dr Baig added that epilepsy could strike at any age, however more than 70 percent of the cases occurs in first twenty years of life. A panel of Consultant Neurologists including Dr Farah Minhas, Dr Tehseen Muzaffar and Dr Nadir Ali Syed conducted a question and answer session 

Labeling epilepsy as a major health problem in Pakistan. Dr Baig said it is a very common neurological disorder and can occur at any age and is present in several different forms. The causes for epilepsy vary with age and for more than 66 percent of the cases, there is no known cause for occurrence of this disease. Highlighting the importance of earlv diagnosis for epilepsy, Dr Baig revealed that "if the disorder is recognized at an early stage, then in up to 70 percent of the cases, complete recover is possible with appropriate medication" He stressed that the treatment has to be continued in appropriate dosage under strict supervision of a neurologist. 

Commenting on facts and fiction about the epilepsy, Dr Baig informed that there are absolutely no medical restrictions for epileptic patients to get married and live a normal life.
